body: I'd like to take a look at this one if no one has objections - want to familiarize myself more with the core code
Sure, this should be pretty straight-forward, I think.

Finally got around to looking at this and am finding myself confused - what is the desired behavior? According to http://eslint.org/blog/2015/09/eslint-v1.4.0-released, it seems like it's working as intended - the cache is deleted when ESLint is run without the `--cache` flag. If that isn't the intended behavior, what is? Thanks in advance!
Since the cache only has meaning when ESLint is run on files, maybe there's no need to wipe the cache when `--stdin` option is passed to CLI. At least, that's my take on it.

Yes, that's right. Deletion should move inside executeOnFiles.

What about when `--stdin-filename` is used? Any difference there?

I would say no, that should not make a difference.  When `--stdin-filename` is used, we still call `executeOnText`, which bypasses all of the cache application logic.  There's no chance in _using_ a cache when linting straight text, so I argue that it also should not be _deleting_ the cache either.

To give a little more explanation, I run eslint in my editor (Atom), which lints using `--stdin` and `--stdin-filename`.  Linting there is quick, because it only runs on one file-worth of text at a time.  When I'm ready to commit changes, I run an npm script which lints the entire codebase with `--cache`.  I would like the cache to persist between my `npm run lint` executions, because without it linting can take quite a while.
Opened a PR - thanks for letting me take this on :) Most of my work has been in rules so far, and I'm eager to get to know the core code better!
